subject.title: Managed hook resources survive handler reloads

question: Should managed and workspace internal-hook modules be allowed to own long-running process resources through a new disposal lifecycle, or should those resources remain plugin-service responsibilities?
rationale: Both directions are technically viable, but adding `dispose` expands the public hook-module contract and overlaps an existing plugin lifecycle surface; repository policy alone cannot establish the intended product boundary.

options.title: Keep resources in plugins
options.body: Document internal hooks as lightweight handlers and direct timers, watchers, sockets, and clients to plugin gateway lifecycle hooks.

options.title: Add hook disposal
options.body: Define and document an optional async `dispose` export with once-per-module, reverse-order, error-isolated cleanup on reload, disable, and shutdown.

recommendation.title: Keep resources in plugins
recommendation.body: Document internal hooks as lightweight handlers and direct timers, watchers, sockets, and clients to plugin gateway lifecycle hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the commit that introduced the current reset-and-reload registration lifecycle.
